\section{Auxiliary order-eight Laurent coefficient certificate}%
\label{app:order-eight-laurent-certificate}

This appendix gives the finite certificate for the order-eight rows used to
audit the \(A_8\) substitution.  The main coefficient hierarchy has already
been proved in Section~\ref{sec:entropy-asymptotics}; the material below is
a reproducible check of one explicit example.  The single convention is
\[
q_{n,k}=2^{-n}(-\ii)^n
\operatorname{sgn}(k)^{\,n\bmod2}
\binom{n-1}{|k|-1},
\qquad 0<|k|\le n,
\]
and
\[
J(n_1,\ldots,n_r)=[z^0]\prod_{j=1}^rQ_{n_j}(z).
\]

The Laurent representatives used in the rows through total order eight are
\begin{align}
Q_2(z)
&=-\frac14\bigl(z+z^{-1}+z^2+z^{-2}\bigr),
\label{eq:appendix-d-explicit-q2}\\
Q_3(z)
&=\frac{\ii}{8}\bigl((z-z^{-1})+2(z^2-z^{-2})+(z^3-z^{-3})\bigr),
\label{eq:appendix-d-explicit-q3}\\
Q_4(z)
&=\frac1{16}\bigl((z+z^{-1})+3(z^2+z^{-2})
  +3(z^3+z^{-3})+(z^4+z^{-4})\bigr),
\label{eq:appendix-d-explicit-q4}\\
Q_5(z)
&=-\frac{\ii}{32}\bigl((z-z^{-1})+4(z^2-z^{-2})
  +6(z^3-z^{-3})+4(z^4-z^{-4})+(z^5-z^{-5})\bigr),
\label{eq:appendix-d-explicit-q5}\\
Q_6(z)
&=-\frac1{64}\bigl((z+z^{-1})+5(z^2+z^{-2})
  +10(z^3+z^{-3})+10(z^4+z^{-4}) \nonumber\\
&\hspace{6.7em}
  +5(z^5+z^{-5})+(z^6+z^{-6})\bigr).
\label{eq:appendix-d-explicit-q6}
\end{align}
These are exactly the cases \(2\le n\le6\) of
\eqref{eq:mode-laurent-polynomial-definition}.  They are displayed so that
the signs in the odd negative-exponent rows can be checked directly.

For a Laurent polynomial \(F(z)=\sum_{|k|\le K}a_kz^k\), put
\[
\mathsf G_N(F):=\frac1N\sum_{\ell=0}^{N-1}F(\zeta_N^\ell),
\qquad \zeta_N:=e^{2\pi\ii/N}.
\]
If \(N>K\), then \(\mathsf G_N(F)=[z^0]F\).  Thus the following exact
root-of-unity checks extract the same constant terms without using the
zero-sum recurrence:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{object}&\text{value}\\
\hline
Q_2(1),Q_2(-1)&-1,\ 0\\
Q_3(1),Q_3(-1)&0,\ 0\\
Q_4(1),Q_4(-1)&1,\ 0\\
Q_5(1),Q_5(-1)&0,\ 0\\
Q_6(1),Q_6(-1)&-1,\ 0\\
\mathsf G_{17}(Q_2Q_6)&3/64\\
\mathsf G_{17}(Q_3Q_5)&-15/128\\
\mathsf G_{17}(Q_2Q_3^2)&-9/128 .
\end{array}
\]
The grid checks are exact finite averages, since
\(17>2+6=3+5=2+3+3\).

\begin{lemma}[Deterministic exact Laurent recurrence]%
\label{lem:appendix-d-deterministic-laurent-recurrence}
Let \(\mathbf n=(n_1,\ldots,n_r)\) be any finite row of positive integers.
Define finitely supported maps \(C_j:\ZZ\to\QQ[\ii]\) by
\[
C_0(s)=\mathbf 1_{\{s=0\}},\qquad
C_j(s)=\sum_{0<|k|\le n_j}
2^{-n_j}(-\ii)^{n_j}\operatorname{sgn}(k)^{\,n_j\bmod2}
\binom{n_j-1}{|k|-1}\,C_{j-1}(s-k).
\]
Then
\[
  C_r(0)=[z^0]\prod_{j=1}^r Q_{n_j}(z)=J(\mathbf n).
\]
Equivalently, with
\[
\mathcal K(\mathbf n)
:=\{(k_1,\ldots,k_r):0<|k_j|\le n_j,\ k_1+\cdots+k_r=0\}
\]
and \(\lambda_n:=2^{-n}(-\ii)^n\),
\[
C_r(0)=
\prod_{j=1}^r\lambda_{n_j}
\sum_{\mathbf k\in\mathcal K(\mathbf n)}
\prod_{j=1}^r
\operatorname{sgn}(k_j)^{\,n_j\bmod2}
\binom{n_j-1}{|k_j|-1}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The coefficient formula \eqref{eq:mode-laurent-coefficients} says that
multiplication by \(Q_{n_j}\) sends a coefficient array \(C_{j-1}\) to the
convolution array displayed above.  Induction on \(j\) gives
\[
  C_j(s)=[z^s]\prod_{a=1}^jQ_{n_a}(z),
\]
and hence \(C_r(0)\) is the desired constant term.  Expanding the last
coefficient and collecting the common factor
\(\prod_j\lambda_{n_j}\) gives the zero-sum formula.
\end{proof}

The row certificate is the following finite table: \(S(\mathbf n)\) is the
integer zero-sum convolution in
Lemma~\ref{lem:appendix-d-deterministic-laurent-recurrence}, and
\(J(\mathbf n)=\Lambda(\mathbf n)S(\mathbf n)\), where
\(\Lambda(\mathbf n)=\prod_j\lambda_{n_j}\).
\[
\begin{array}{c|r|r|c|c}
\mathbf n&|\mathcal K(\mathbf n)|&S(\mathbf n)&\Lambda(\mathbf n)&J(\mathbf n)\\
\hline
(2,6)&4&12&1/256&3/64\\
(3,5)&6&-30&1/256&-15/128\\
(4,4)&8&40&1/256&5/32\\
(2,2,4)&12&24&1/256&3/32\\
(2,3,3)&14&-18&1/256&-9/128\\
(2,2,2,2)&36&36&1/256&9/64 .
\end{array}
\]
Odd total-order entries through order eight vanish by
\(u_n(-y)=(-1)^nu_n(y)\).  The sign-sensitive rows
\((3,5)\) and \((2,3,3)\) use the same all-sign coefficient rule as the
other rows; no separate conjugation convention is applied.

As a model for the sign-sensitive rows, write
\[
w_n(k):=\operatorname{sgn}(k)^{\,n\bmod 2}
\binom{n-1}{|k|-1},\qquad 0<|k|\le n .
\]
For \((3,5)\), the zero-sum condition forces the second index to be \(-k\).
Hence
\[
S(3,5)
=\sum_{0<|k|\le3}w_3(k)w_5(-k).
\]
Since \(\operatorname{sgn}(-k)=-\operatorname{sgn}(k)\), the two choices
\(k=\pm r\), \(r=1,2,3\), contribute the same negative weight:
\[
S(3,5)
=-2\left[
\binom20\binom40+\binom21\binom41+\binom22\binom42
\right]
=-2(1+8+6)=-30.
\]
The rational prefactor is
\(\Lambda(3,5)=\lambda_3\lambda_5=(\ii/8)(-\ii/32)=1/256\), and therefore
\[
J(3,5)=-\frac{30}{256}=-\frac{15}{128}.
\]
The row \((2,3,3)\) is obtained from the same recurrence with no change of
sign convention.

Finally, the order-eight coefficient substitution is obtained by inserting
the six row values into the universal entropy coefficient:
\[
\begin{aligned}
A_8&=\mu_2\mu_6J(2,6)+\mu_3\mu_5J(3,5)
+\frac12\mu_4^2J(4,4)
-\frac12\mu_2^2\mu_4J(2,2,4)\\
&\hspace{2.5em}
-\frac12\mu_2\mu_3^2J(2,3,3)
+\frac1{12}\mu_2^4J(2,2,2,2).
\end{aligned}
\]
With \(\mu_2=\sigma^2\), this gives
\[
A_8=
\frac{3\sigma^8-12\sigma^4\mu_4+9\sigma^2\mu_3^2
+12\sigma^2\mu_6-30\mu_3\mu_5+20\mu_4^2}{256}.
\]
This appendix is therefore a compact reproducibility certificate for the
finite Laurent rows and the coefficient substitution.  It is not an
additional hypothesis and does not replace the main-text coefficient theorem.

\begin{remark}
This rigidity statement is only for the coefficient layer through order eight proved in
this paper.  No all-order defect hierarchy is asserted here.
\end{remark}

\begin{proof}
Use the notation of Corollaries~\ref{thm:poisson-defect-ladder}
and~\ref{thm:poisson-defect-amplification}.  From
\eqref{eq:defect-c6},
\[
A_6(\nu)+\frac{7}{64}\sigma^6
=-\frac{\sigma^6}{32}\beta_3^2-\frac{\sigma^6}{8}\kappa
\le0,
\qquad
\kappa:=\|Q_2\|_{L^2(\nu)}^2.
\]
Hence \(A_6(\nu)\) is maximized by, and only by, laws for which
$\beta_3=0$ and $\kappa=0$.  In that case
$Q_2=X^2-1$ vanishes almost surely, so $X=\pm1$ almost surely; since
$\EE X=0$ and $\EE X^2=1$, the two signs have equal mass.  This is exactly
$\nu_c=\rho_\sigma$.  Conversely, for $\nu_c=\rho_\sigma$ one has
$\beta_3=0$ and $Q_2=0$, so equality holds in the displayed bound for
\(A_6(\nu)\).

The lower bound for \(A_8(\nu)\) and the characterization of equality
in that bound are precisely \eqref{eq:defect-c8-lower} and the equality
statement in Corollary~\ref{thm:poisson-defect-ladder}.  The definitions of
\(\Delta_6\) and \(\mathcal E_8\) convert equality
in the two coefficient bounds into
\(\Delta_6(\nu)=0\) and
\(\mathcal E_8(\nu)=0\), respectively.  Finally,
Corollary~\ref{thm:poisson-defect-amplification} states that equality in
\[
\mathcal E_8(\nu)\ge
\frac{13\sigma^2}{8}\Delta_6(\nu)
\]
holds if and only if $\nu_c=\rho_\sigma$.  Combining these equivalences
proves all the listed conditions equivalent.
\end{proof}
\endinput

There is a constant \\(C_q\\) such that\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:critical-bregman-pointwise-bound}\n 0\\le \\Phi(u+v)-\\Phi(u)-\\log(1+u)v\\le C_q|v|^q\n\\end{equation}\nwhenever \\(|u|\\le1/4\\) and \\(u+v\\ge-1\\).\n\\end{lemma}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nThe lower bound is convexity.  If \\(|v|\\le1/2\\), the segment between\n\\(u\\) and \\(u+v\\) is contained in \\([-3/4,3/4]\\).  Since\n\\(\\Phi\u0027\u0027(s)=(1+s)^{-1}\\) there, Taylor\u0027s theorem gives an upper bound\n\\(C v^2\\le C|v|^q\\).  If \\(v\u003c-1/2\\), the admissible pairs\n\\((u,v)\\) range over a compact set and \\(|v|^q\\ge2^{-q}\\); continuity at\n\\(u+v=-1\\) gives the result.  If \\(v\u003e1/2\\), direct expansion of the left\nside shows that it is at most \\(C(1+v)\\log(1+v)+Cv\\), which is bounded by\n\\(C_qv^q\\).  These three regions prove\n\\eqref{eq:critical-bregman-pointwise-bound}.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\section{Optimal first-unmatched-moment asymptotics}\n\n\\begin{theorem}[Optimal uniform sufficient moment exponent for stable KL asymptotics]\n\\label{thm:high-dimensional-kl-moment-threshold}\nLet \\(d\\ge1\\), \\(0\u003c\\alpha\u003c2\\), and let \\(\\nu\\) be a probability law on\n\\(\\RR^d\\) with mean \\(\\bar\\gamma\\).  Put\n\\(X=\\gamma-\\bar\\gamma\\), and assume\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:critical-kl-moment-hypothesis}\n \\EE|X|^{p_{\\alpha,d}}\u003c\\infty,\n \\qquad\n p_{\\alpha,d}=\\max\\left\\{2,\n \\frac{4(d+\\alpha)}{d+\\alpha+4}\\right\\},\n\\end{equation}\nthen the covariance \\(\\Sigma=\\EE[XX^{\\mathsf T}]\\) is finite and\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:critical-kl-leading-asymptotic}\n H_{\\alpha,d}(s):=\n D_{\\rm KL}\\!\\left(p_s^{(\\alpha,d)}*\\nu\\,\\middle\\|\\,\n p_s^{(\\alpha,d)}(\\mathord\\cdot-\\bar\\gamma)\\right)\n =\\mathcal Q_{\\alpha,d}(\\Sigma)s^{-4}+o(s^{-4}),\n\\end{equation}\nwhere\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:stable-leading-covariance-functional}\n b_{\\alpha,d,\\Sigma}(y)\n :=\\frac1{2p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(y)}\n   \\sum_{i,j=1}^d\\Sigma_{ij}\\partial_{ij}p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(y),\n \\qquad\n \\mathcal Q_{\\alpha,d}(\\Sigma)\n :=\\frac12\\int b_{\\alpha,d,\\Sigma}^2\\dd\\Omega_{\\alpha,d}.\n\\end{equation}\nThe exponent is optimal only in the following uniform sense.  For every\n\\(0\u003cr\u003c2\\), there is a mean-zero law with finite \\(r\\)th absolute moment\nand \\(\\limsup_{s\\to\\infty}s^4H_{\\alpha,d}(s)=+\\infty\\).  If\n\\(d+\\alpha\u003e4\\), then for every \\(2\\le r\u003cp_{\\alpha,d}\\) the counterexample\nmay additionally be chosen with positive-definite finite covariance.\nThus no smaller moment exponent implies\n\\eqref{eq:critical-kl-leading-asymptotic} uniformly over its entire moment\nclass, and the endpoint belongs to the sufficient side.\n\nThis is not a law-by-law moment criterion.  When \\(d+\\alpha\u003e4\\), finite\n\\(p_{\\alpha,d}\\)-moment is not asserted to be necessary for an individual\nlaw; the exact finite-covariance criterion is the nonlinear raw-tail energy\nin Theorem~\\ref{thm:stable-law-by-law-decomposition} below.  When\n\\(d+\\alpha\\le4\\), the exponent is two and boundedness of\n\\(s^4H_{\\alpha,d}(s)\\) does force finite covariance, as the proof below\nshows.  For \\(\\alpha=1\\) with the standard normalization\n\\(p_1^{(1,d)}=P_1^{(d)}\\), one has\n\\(\\mathcal Q_{1,d}=\\mathcal Q_d\\), so the theorem contains the radial\nPoisson result above.\n\\end{theorem}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nTranslation permits us to assume \\(\\bar\\gamma=0\\).  Fix\n\\(q=q_{\\alpha,d}\\), \\(p=p_{\\alpha,d}\\), and \\(m=\\lfloor p\\rfloor\\),\nand write\n\\[\n R_m(y,z)=F_y^{(\\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\\alpha,d)}(y,z),\n \\qquad r_s(y)=\\EE R_m(y,X/s).\n\\]\nMinkowski\u0027s inequality and\n\\eqref{eq:stable-critical-global-remainder} give\n\\[\n s^p\\|R_m(\\cdot,X/s)\\|_q\\le C_{\\alpha,d}|X|^p.\n\\]\nFor each fixed \\(X\\), the local part of the same estimate and \\(m+1\u003ep\\)\ngive\n\\[\n s^p\\|R_m(\\cdot,X/s)\\|_q\n \\le C_{\\alpha,d}|X|^{m+1}s^{p-m-1}\\longrightarrow0.\n\\]\nDominated convergence therefore yields\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:critical-lq-integrated-remainder}\n \\|r_s\\|_{L^q(\\Omega_{\\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-p}).\n\\end{equation}\n\nCentering removes the linear Taylor layer.  Averaging the remaining layers\ngives\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:critical-kl-quotient-decomposition}\n \\delta_s^{(\\alpha,d)}=u_s+r_s,\n \\qquad\n u_s=s^{-2}b_{\\alpha,d,\\Sigma}\n       +\\mathbf 1_{\\{m=3\\}}s^{-3}B_3,\n\\end{equation}\nwhere \\(B_3\\) is a bounded linear combination of third-order modes.  In the\nsecond case the required third moments exist because \\(p\\ge3\\).  Hence\n\\(\\|u_s\\|_\\infty=O(s^{-2})\\).  The boundedness of all these modes follows\nfrom Proposition~\\ref{prop:stable-kernel-input-package}.\n\nThe identity\n\\(F_y^{(\\alpha,d)}(z)\\Omega_{\\alpha,d}(\\dd y)\n=p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(y-z)\\dd y\\) shows that every translated quotient has\nintegral one.  Moreover,\n\\(\\int|F_y^{(\\alpha,d)}(z)-1|\\Omega_{\\alpha,d}(\\dd y)\\le2\\), so Tonelli\u0027s\ntheorem gives \\(\\delta_s^{(\\alpha,d)}\\in L^1(\\Omega_{\\alpha,d})\\) with\nzero integral.  The KL change of variables is therefore\n\\[\n H_{\\alpha,d}(s)=\\int\\Phi(\\delta_s^{(\\alpha,d)})\\dd\\Omega_{\\alpha,d}\n\\]\nin the extended sense.  For all sufficiently large \\(s\\), apply\nLemma~\\ref{lem:critical-lq-kl-perturbation} to \\(u=u_s\\), \\(v=r_s\\).\nHölder\u0027s inequality and \\eqref{eq:critical-lq-integrated-remainder} give\n\\begin{align*}\n \\left|H_{\\alpha,d}(s)-\\int\\Phi(u_s)\\dd\\Omega_{\\alpha,d}\\right|\n \u0026\\le \\|\\log(1+u_s)\\|_{q/(q-1)}\\|r_s\\|_q\n       +C_q\\|r_s\\|_q^q\\\\\n \u0026\\le O(s^{-2})o(s^{-p})+o(s^{-pq})=o(s^{-4}),\n\\end{align*}\nbecause \\(p\\ge2\\) and \\(pq=4\\).\nThis estimate also proves that the extended KL integral is finite for all\nsufficiently large \\(s\\).\n\nFinally, the boundedness of the retained modes permits a uniform Taylor\nexpansion of \\(\\Phi(u_s)\\).  From\n\\eqref{eq:critical-kl-quotient-decomposition},\n\\[\n \\int\\Phi(u_s)\\dd\\Omega_{\\alpha,d}\n =\\frac{s^{-4}}2\\int b_{\\alpha,d,\\Sigma}^2\\dd\\Omega_{\\alpha,d}\n   +o(s^{-4})\n =\\mathcal Q_{\\alpha,d}(\\Sigma)s^{-4}+o(s^{-4}),\n\\]\nwhich proves \\eqref{eq:critical-kl-leading-asymptotic}.\n\nWe first prove the obstruction below two moments.  If\n\\(\\limsup_{s\\to\\infty}s^4H_{\\alpha,d}(s)\u003c\\infty\\), Pinsker\u0027s inequality\nand scaling give, for every fixed \\(\\xi\\in\\RR^d\\),\n\\[\n |\\widehat p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(\\xi)|\n |\\varphi_X(\\xi/s)-1|\n \\le \\|p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}*\\nu_s-p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}\\|_1\n \\le \\sqrt{2H_{\\alpha,d}(s)}=O(s^{-2}),\n\\]\nwhere \\(\\nu_s\\) is the law of \\(X/s\\).  Since the stable characteristic\nfunction never vanishes, take \\(\\xi=e\\) for a unit vector \\(e\\), multiply\nthe real part by \\(s^2\\), and use Fatou\u0027s lemma to obtain\n\\[\n \\frac12\\EE(e\\cdot X)^2\n \\le \\liminf_{s\\to\\infty}s^2\n       \\EE[1-\\cos((e\\cdot X)/s)]\u003c\\infty.\n\\]\nThus bounded scaled entropy forces finite covariance.  Given \\(0\u003cr\u003c2\\),\nchoose \\(a\\in(\\max\\{1,r\\},2)\\) and put symmetric masses proportional to\n\\(n^{-a-1}\\) at \\(\\pm ne_1\\), with the remaining mass at zero.  This law\nhas mean zero and finite \\(r\\)th moment but infinite variance, so its scaled\nentropy has infinite limsup.\n\nIt remains to prove optimality between two and \\(p\\) when \\(\\beta\u003e4\\).\nFix \\(2\\le r\u003cp\\), choose positive \\(a_j\\) with \\(\\sum_ja_j\u003c\\infty\\), and\nput symmetric masses \\(w_j/2\\) at \\(\\pm R_je_1\\), where\n\\(w_j=a_jR_j^{-r}\\).  Add a sufficiently small bounded symmetric spanning\ncomponent.  The resulting law has positive-definite finite covariance and\nfinite \\(r\\)th moment.  Set\n\\[\n s_j=\\kappa R_jw_j^{1/\\beta},\\qquad\n A_j=B(R_je_1,s_j).\n\\]\nThe component at \\(R_je_1\\) gives\n\\((p_{s_j}^{(\\alpha,d)}*\\nu)(A_j)\\ge c_{\\alpha,d}w_j\\).  On the other hand,\n\\eqref{eq:stable-input-density} and \\(s_j/R_j\\to0\\) give\n\\[\n p_{s_j}^{(\\alpha,d)}(A_j)\n \\le C_{\\alpha,d}(s_j/R_j)^\\beta\n =C_{\\alpha,d}\\kappa^\\beta w_j.\n\\]\nChoose \\(\\kappa\\) so that\n\\(C_{\\alpha,d}\\kappa^\\beta\u003cc_{\\alpha,d}\\).  Data processing to\n\\(\\{A_j,A_j^c\\}\\) and\nLemma~\\ref{lem:bernoulli-kl-linear-separation} then yield\n\\(H_{\\alpha,d}(s_j)\\ge c w_j\\), and hence\n\\[\n s_j^4H_{\\alpha,d}(s_j)\n \\ge cR_j^4w_j^{1+4/\\beta}\n =ca_j^{q_{\\alpha,d}}R_j^{4-rq_{\\alpha,d}}.\n\\]\nHere \\(q_{\\alpha,d}=1+4/\\beta\\) and\n\\(r\u003cp=4/q_{\\alpha,d}\\), so the exponent of \\(R_j\\) is positive.\nRecursive choice of the radii makes \\(s_j\\to\\infty\\) and the last display\nunbounded while preserving all moment assertions.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{lemma}[All-order stable critical remainder]\n\\label{lem:all-order-stable-critical-remainder}\nLet \\(r\\ge1\\), put \\(\\beta=d+\\alpha\\), and define\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:all-order-stable-critical-exponents}\n q_{r,\\alpha,d}:=\\min\\left\\{2,1+\\frac{2r}{d+\\alpha}\\right\\},\n \\qquad\n p_{r,\\alpha,d}:=\\frac{2r}{q_{r,\\alpha,d}}\n =\\max\\left\\{r,\\frac{2r(d+\\alpha)}{d+\\alpha+2r}\\right\\}.\n\\end{equation}\nLet \\(q=q_{r,\\alpha,d}\\), \\(p=p_{r,\\alpha,d}\\), and\n\\(m=\\lfloor p\\rfloor\\).  If \\(T_m^{(\\alpha,d)}(y,z)\\) is the Taylor\npolynomial of \\(F_y^{(\\alpha,d)}(z)\\) at zero through degree \\(m\\), then\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:all-order-stable-critical-remainder}\n \\|F_\\cdot^{(\\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\\alpha,d)}(\\cdot,z)\\|_{L^q(\\Omega_{\\alpha,d})}\n \\le C_{\\alpha,d,r}\n \\begin{cases}\n  |z|^{m+1},\u0026|z|\\le1,\\\\\n  |z|^p,\u0026|z|\u003e1,\n \\end{cases}\n \\le C_{\\alpha,d,r}|z|^p.\n\\end{equation}\nConsequently, if a probability law \\(\\lambda\\) on \\(\\RR^d\\) has finite\n\\(p\\)th absolute moment and\n\\[\n q_s^\\lambda(y):=\\int F_y^{(\\alpha,d)}(x/s)\\lambda(\\dd x),\n\\]\nthen\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:all-order-stable-integrated-remainder}\n q_s^\\lambda\n =1+\\sum_{j=1}^m s^{-j}B_j^\\lambda+r_s^\\lambda,\n \\qquad\n \\|r_s^\\lambda\\|_{L^q(\\Omega_{\\alpha,d})}=o(s^{-p}),\n\\end{equation}\nwhere\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:all-order-stable-moment-modes}\n B_j^\\lambda(y):=\n \\frac{(-1)^j}{p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(y)}\n \\sum_{|\\gamma|=j}\\frac{m_\\gamma(\\lambda)}{\\gamma!}\n \\partial^\\gamma p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(y),\n \\qquad\n m_\\gamma(\\lambda):=\\int x^\\gamma\\lambda(\\dd x).\n\\end{equation}\nEvery \\(B_j^\\lambda\\) in this display is bounded.\n\\end{lemma}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nThe proof of \\eqref{eq:stable-translation-lq-growth} applies verbatim for\nevery fixed \\(1\u003cq\\le2\\) and gives\n\\[\n \\|F_\\cdot^{(\\alpha,d)}(z)\\|_{L^q(\\Omega_{\\alpha,d})}\n \\le C(1+|z|)^{\\beta(1-1/q)}.\n\\]\nThe local Taylor argument in the proof of\nLemma~\\ref{lem:stable-critical-translation-remainder} gives the first line\nof \\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-critical-remainder}.  For \\(|z|\u003e1\\), the\nTaylor modes are bounded by\nProposition~\\ref{prop:stable-kernel-input-package}, and\nhence\n\\[\n \\|F_\\cdot^{(\\alpha,d)}(z)-T_m^{(\\alpha,d)}(\\cdot,z)\\|_q\n \\le C\\{|z|^{\\beta(1-1/q)}+|z|^m\\}\\le C|z|^p.\n\\]\nIndeed, \\(m\\le p\\), while\n\\(\\beta(1-1/q)\\le p\\); in the non-Hilbert regime\n\\(\\beta\u003e2r\\), both sides of the latter inequality equal\n\\(2r\\beta/(\\beta+2r)\\).  Since \\(m+1\u003ep\\), the final inequality in\n\\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-critical-remainder} also holds on the unit ball.\n\nTaylor\u0027s formula gives \\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-integrated-remainder}\nbefore its norm assertion.  For fixed \\(x\\), the local estimate implies\n\\[\n s^p\\|F_\\cdot^{(\\alpha,d)}(x/s)\n       -T_m^{(\\alpha,d)}(\\cdot,x/s)\\|_q\\longrightarrow0,\n\\]\nwhereas \\eqref{eq:all-order-stable-critical-remainder} bounds this expression\nby \\(C|x|^p\\).  Minkowski\u0027s inequality and dominated convergence prove the\nclaimed \\(L^q\\) remainder.  Boundedness of the modes follows again from\nProposition~\\ref{prop:stable-kernel-input-package}.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{lemma}[Two-background critical Bregman transfer]\n\\label{lem:two-background-critical-bregman-transfer}\nLet \\(1\u003cq\\le2\\), \\(p\\ge r\u003e0\\), and \\(pq=2r\\).  On a probability space\n\\((E,\\Omega)\\), suppose \\(g_s\\ge c_s\u003e0\\),\n\\[\n \\int g_s\\dd\\Omega=1,\\qquad c_s\\longrightarrow1,\n \\qquad \\|g_s-1\\|_{L^1(\\Omega)}\\longrightarrow0.\n\\]\nLet \\(B\\in L^\\infty(\\Omega)\\), and suppose\n\\[\n v_s=s^{-r}B+o(s^{-r})\\quad\\hbox{in }L^\\infty(\\Omega),\n \\qquad \\|e_s\\|_{L^q(\\Omega)}=o(s^{-p}).\n\\]\nIf \\(g_s+v_s+e_s\\ge0\\) and both \\(g_s\\Omega\\) and\n\\((g_s+v_s+e_s)\\Omega\\) are probability measures, then\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:two-background-critical-bregman-transfer}\n D_{\\rm KL}((g_s+v_s+e_s)\\Omega\\|g_s\\Omega)\n =\\frac{s^{-2r}}2\\int B^2\\dd\\Omega+o(s^{-2r}).\n\\end{equation}\n\\end{lemma}\n\nThe hypotheses on the denominator in this lemma deliberately stop short of\n\\(L^\\infty\\)-convergence to one.  They require only a positive lower bound\napproaching one, mass normalization, and \\(L^1\\)-convergence.  This weaker\ninterface is what permits a heavy-tailed translated mixture to serve as the\nbackground.\n\n\\begin{proof}\nFor \\(g\u003e0\\), write \\(\\Psi_g(z)=g\\Phi(z/g)\\).  Scaling\nLemma~\\ref{lem:critical-lq-kl-perturbation} shows, whenever\n\\(|v/g|\\le1/4\\) and \\(g+v+e\\ge0\\), that\n\\[\n 0\\le\\Psi_g(v+e)-\\Psi_g(v)\n      -\\log(1+v/g)e\\le C_q g^{1-q}|e|^q.\n\\]\nFor large \\(s\\), the hypotheses give \\(g_s\\ge1/2\\) and\n\\(\\|v_s/g_s\\|_\\infty\\le1/4\\).  Therefore H\\\"older\u0027s inequality yields\n\\begin{align*}\n \u0026\\left|D_{\\rm KL}((g_s+v_s+e_s)\\Omega\\|g_s\\Omega)\n       -\\int\\Psi_{g_s}(v_s)\\dd\\Omega\\right|\\\\\n \u0026\\qquad\\le\n C\\|v_s\\|_{L^{q/(q-1)}}\\|e_s\\|_{L^q}\n +C\\|e_s\\|_{L^q}^q\n =o(s^{-r-p})+o(s^{-pq})=o(s^{-2r}).\n\\end{align*}\nUniform Taylor expansion at zero gives\n\\[\n \\int\\Psi_{g_s}(v_s)\\dd\\Omega\n =\\frac12\\int\\frac{v_s^2}{g_s}\\dd\\Omega+O(\\|v_s\\|_\\infty^3).\n\\]\nFinally,\n\\[\n \\left|\\int B^2(g_s^{-1}-1)\\dd\\Omega\\right|\n \\le2\\|B\\|_\\infty^2\\|g_s-1\\|_1\\longrightarrow0,\n\\]\nand \\eqref{eq:two-background-critical-bregman-transfer} follows.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{lemma}[Finite-difference moment blocks]\n\\label{lem:stable-finite-difference-blocks}\nLet \\(r\\ge1\\), let \\(e\\) be a unit vector, and define\n\\[\n \\sigma_R:=2^{1-r}\\sum_{k=0}^r(-1)^{r-k}\\binom rk\n                 \\delta_{(k+1)Re}=A_R^+-A_R^-.\n\\]\nThen \\(A_R^+\\) and \\(A_R^-\\) are probability measures and\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:stable-block-moment-identities}\n \\int x^\\gamma\\dd\\sigma_R(x)=0\\quad(|\\gamma|\u003cr),\n \\qquad\n \\int(e\\cdot x)^r\\dd\\sigma_R(x)=2^{1-r}r!R^r.\n\\end{equation}\n\\end{lemma}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nThe positive and negative binomial coefficients each sum to \\(2^{r-1}\\),\nand the order-\\(r\\) forward-difference identity gives\n\\eqref{eq:stable-block-moment-identities}.  In particular, when \\(r=1\\),\n\\(\\sigma_R=\\delta_{2Re}-\\delta_{Re}\\); the same cancellation and nonzero\nfirst-difference conclusions hold without a separate construction.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{lemma}[Moving-ball probability separation]\n\\label{lem:stable-moving-ball-probability-separation}\nLet \\(\\beta=d+\\alpha\\), let \\(A_R^\\pm\\) be the blocks in\nLemma~\\ref{lem:stable-finite-difference-blocks}, and suppose\n\\[\n R_{j+1}\u003e4(r+1)R_j,\n \\qquad w_j\u003e0,\n \\qquad \\sum_jw_j\u003c1.\n\\]\nDefine\n\\[\n \\nu=\\left(1-\\sum_jw_j\\right)\\delta_0+\\sum_jw_jA_{R_j}^+,\n \\qquad\n \\eta=\\left(1-\\sum_jw_j\\right)\\delta_0+\\sum_jw_jA_{R_j}^-.\n\\]\nPut \\(x_j=(r+1)R_je\\), choose\n\\(s_j=\\kappa R_jw_j^{1/\\beta}\u003cR_j/4\\), and set\n\\(E_j=B(x_j,s_j)\\).  There are constants \\(a_r\u003e0\\) and\n\\(C_{\\alpha,d,r}\u003c\\infty\\), independent of \\(j,\\kappa,R_j,w_j\\), such that\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:stable-moving-ball-probability-separation}\n (p_{s_j}^{(\\alpha,d)}*\\nu)(E_j)\\ge a_rw_j,\n \\qquad\n (p_{s_j}^{(\\alpha,d)}*\\eta)(E_j)\n \\le C_{\\alpha,d,r}\\kappa^\\beta w_j.\n\\end{equation}\n\\end{lemma}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nThe endpoint coefficient in \\(A_{R_j}^+\\) at \\(x_j\\) is \\(2^{1-r}\\).\nStable scaling and positivity therefore give\n\\[\n (p_{s_j}^{(\\alpha,d)}*\\nu)(E_j)\n \\ge 2^{1-r}w_j\\int_{B(0,1)}p_1^{(\\alpha,d)}(y)\\dd y\n =:a_rw_j.\n\\]\nWe verify the separation from every atom of \\(\\eta\\).  In block \\(j\\),\nopposite-sign atoms are at least \\(R_j\\) from \\(x_j\\).  Every earlier atom\nhas norm at most \\((r+1)R_{j-1}\u003cR_j/4\\), whereas every later atom has norm at\nleast \\(R_{j+1}\u003e4(r+1)R_j\\); the atom at zero obeys the earlier-atom bound.\nAfter subtracting the radius \\(s_j\u003cR_j/4\\), every such atom \\(z\\) satisfies\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:stable-moving-ball-distance}\n \\operatorname{dist}(z,E_j)\\ge3R_j/4.\n\\end{equation}\nFor \\(y\\in E_j\\), the stable density upper bound and scaling now give\n\\[\n p_{s_j}^{(\\alpha,d)}(y-z)\n \\le C_{\\alpha,d,r}s_j^\\alpha R_j^{-\\beta}.\n\\]\n"

-\label{thm:low-dimensional-finite-covariance-threshold}
-Let \(1\le d\le3\), and let \(\nu\) be a probability law on \(\RR^d\) with
-finite mean.  With
-\[
- H_d(t)=D_{\rm KL}\!\left(P_t^{(d)}*\nu\,\middle\|\,
- P_t^{(d)}(\mathord\cdot-\bar\gamma)\right),
-\]
-one has
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:low-dimensional-covariance-iff}
- \EE|X|^2<\infty
- \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
- \limsup_{t\to\infty}t^4H_d(t)<\infty.
-\end{equation}
-If the covariance is finite, then
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:low-dimensional-covariance-limit}
- H_d(t)=\mathcal Q_d(\Sigma)t^{-4}+o(t^{-4}).
-\end{equation}
-If it is infinite, then \(t^4H_d(t)\to+\infty\) in the extended sense.
-\end{theorem}
-
-\begin{proof}
-For \(d\le3\), \(q_d=2\).  Thus Theorem
-\ref{thm:multidim-l2-moment-threshold} and the \(L^2\) alternative in
-Theorem~\ref{thm:second-order-quotient-kl-coefficient} prove
-\eqref{eq:low-dimensional-covariance-limit}.  The entropy representation is
-valid in the extended sense by change of variables; for large \(t\), the
-\(L^2\) convergence makes \(\Phi(\delta_t^{(d)})\) integrable because
-\(\Phi(s)\le C s^2\) on \([-1,\infty)\).
-
-Conversely, if \(\EE|X|^2=\infty\), some unit vector \(e\) satisfies
-\(\EE(e\cdot X)^2=\infty\).  Projection onto \(e\) sends the radial
-\(d\)-dimensional Poisson law to the one-dimensional Cauchy law at the same
-scale.  The data-processing inequality and
-Theorem~\ref{thm:sharp-leading-kl-variance-threshold} therefore give
-\[
- H_d(t)\ge
- D_{\rm KL}(P_t*\nu_e\|P_t(\mathord\cdot-\bar\gamma_e)),
-\]
-whose product with \(t^4\) tends to \(+\infty\).
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{proposition}[Finite covariance does not control high-dimensional KL]
-\label{prop:high-dimensional-finite-covariance-obstruction}
-For every \(d\ge4\), there exists a centred discrete probability law on
-\(\RR^d\) with positive-definite finite covariance such that
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:high-dimensional-finite-covariance-obstruction}
- \limsup_{t\to\infty}t^4H_d(t)=+\infty.
-\end{equation}
-\end{proposition}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Choose positive \(\alpha_j\) with \(\sum_j\alpha_j<\infty\), radii
-\(R_j\uparrow\infty\), and weights
-\(w_j=\alpha_jR_j^{-2}\).  After rescaling the sequence if necessary,
-\(W=\sum_jw_j<1\).  Begin with
-\[
- (1-W)\delta_0+\sum_{j\ge1}\frac{w_j}{2}
- (\delta_{R_je_1}+\delta_{-R_je_1}),
-\]
-and transfer an arbitrarily small amount of the mass at zero to a bounded
-centred symmetric law spanning \(\RR^d\).  The covariance is then positive
-definite and finite because \(\sum_jw_jR_j^2=\sum_j\alpha_j<\infty\).
-
-Fix a sufficiently small constant \(\kappa>0\), and set
-\[
- t_j=\kappa R_jw_j^{1/(d+1)}.
-\]
-The radii may be chosen recursively so that \(t_j\to\infty\).  Let \(A_j\)
-be the ball of radius \(t_j\) centred at \(R_je_1\).  The \(j\)th mixture
-component gives
-\[
- (P_{t_j}^{(d)}*\nu)(A_j)\ge c_dw_j,
-\]
-whereas, since \(t_j/R_j\to0\), the centred reference satisfies
-\[
- P_{t_j}^{(d)}(A_j)
- \le C_d(t_j/R_j)^{d+1}
- =C_d\kappa^{d+1}w_j.
-\]
-Choose \(\kappa\) so that the second constant is strictly smaller than the
-first.  Data processing to the partition \(\{A_j,A_j^c\}\) and
-Lemma~\ref{lem:bernoulli-kl-linear-separation} then give
-\(H_d(t_j)\ge c'_dw_j\).  Hence
-\[
- t_j^4H_d(t_j)
- \ge c''_dR_j^4w_j^{1+4/(d+1)}
- =c''_d\alpha_j^{1+4/(d+1)}
- R_j^{2(d-3)/(d+1)}.
-\]
-The exponent of \(R_j\) is positive exactly when \(d>3\).  Choosing the
-radii recursively makes the final expression tend to infinity.
-\end{proof}
-
-For the high-dimensional entropy topology, define
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:critical-kl-exponents}
- q_d:=\frac{d+5}{d+1},
- \qquad
- p_d:=\frac{4(d+1)}{d+5}.
-\end{equation}
-Thus \(1<q_d<2\), \(2<p_d<4\), and \(p_dq_d=4\) when \(d\ge4\).
-
-\begin{lemma}[Critical translation remainder]
-\label{lem:critical-lq-translation-remainder}
-Let \(d\ge4\), let \(p_d,q_d\) be as in
-\eqref{eq:critical-kl-exponents}, and put \(m=\lfloor p_d\rfloor\).
-If \(T_m(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of \(F_y(z)\) through degree
-\(m\), then
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:critical-lq-exact-translation-norm}
- \|F_\cdot(z)\|_{L^{q_d}(\Omega_d)}^{q_d}
- =1+\frac{2(d+5)}{(d+1)(d+3)}|z|^2
- +\frac{3}{(d+1)(d+3)}|z|^4.
-\end{equation}
-Consequently, for a constant depending only on \(d\),
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:critical-lq-global-remainder}
- \|F_\cdot(z)-T_m(\cdot,z)\|_{L^{q_d}(\Omega_d)}
- \le C_d
- \begin{cases}
- |z|^{m+1},& |z|\le1,\\
- |z|^{p_d},& |z|>1,
- \end{cases}
- \le C_d|z|^{p_d}.
-\end{equation}
-Here \(m=2\) for \(4\le d\le10\), while \(m=3\) for \(d\ge11\),
-including the integer endpoint \(p_{11}=3\).
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Since \(a(q_d-1)=2\), translation by \(z\) gives
-\[
- \|F_\cdot(z)\|_{q_d}^{q_d}
- =c_d\int_{\RR^d}
- \frac{(1+|u+z|^2)^2}{(1+|u|^2)^{(d+5)/2}}\dd u.
-\]
-Write \(A=1+|u|^2\).  The odd term in the expansion of
-\((A+|z|^2+2u\cdot z)^2\) integrates to zero, and rotational invariance
-gives
-\[
- \int(u\cdot z)^2(1+|u|^2)^{-(d+5)/2}\dd u
- =\frac{|z|^2}{d}\int |u|^2(1+|u|^2)^{-(d+5)/2}\dd u.
-\]
-The three normalized beta integrals needed here are
-\[
- \begin{aligned}
- c_d\int(1+|u|^2)^{-(d+1)/2}\dd u&=1,\\
- c_d\int(1+|u|^2)^{-(d+3)/2}\dd u&=\frac1{d+1},\\
- c_d\int(1+|u|^2)^{-(d+5)/2}\dd u
- &=\frac3{(d+1)(d+3)}.
- \end{aligned}
-\]
-Substitution proves \eqref{eq:critical-lq-exact-translation-norm}.
-
-For \(|z|\le1\), the local quotient--Taylor estimate
-\eqref{eq:local-multidim-taylor-remainder} implies the first line of
-\eqref{eq:critical-lq-global-remainder}.  For \(|z|>1\), the exact identity
-gives \(\|F_\cdot(z)\|_{q_d}\le C_d|z|^{4/q_d}=C_d|z|^{p_d}\).
-Every coefficient of \(T_m\) is bounded in \(y\), and \(m\le p_d\), so
-\(\|T_m(\cdot,z)\|_{q_d}\le C_d|z|^{p_d}\).  Finally,
-\(m+1>p_d\), which proves the last inequality for \(|z|\le1\).
-\end{proof}

Its role\nis only to illustrate how the sixth-order coefficient \\(A_6\\) can be read as\na simple algebraic defect after normalizing to unit variance.  The proof\nbelow supplies the elementary coupling estimate underlying the\nfourth-moment discussion; it uses no finite-time KL estimate and no\neighth-order coefficient.\n\n\\begin{lemma}[Normalized fourth-moment defect algebra]%\n\\label{lem:appendix-normalized-fourth-moment-defect-algebra}\nLet \\(X\\) be a real random variable with \\(\\EE X=0\\), \\(\\EE X^2=1\\), and\n\\(\\EE X^4\u003c\\infty\\).  Put\n\\[\n\\beta_3=\\EE X^3,\\qquad\nQ_2=X^2-1-\\beta_3X,\\qquad\n\\kappa=\\EE Q_2^2,\\qquad\n\\eta=\\frac{\\beta_3^2}{32}+\\frac{\\kappa}{8}.\n\\]\nThen\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:appendix-normalized-fourth-moment-algebra}\n\\eta\n=\\frac{\\beta_3^2}{32}+\\frac{\\EE(X^2-1-\\beta_3X)^2}{8}\n=\\frac{\\EE X^4-1}{8}-\\frac{3\\beta_3^2}{32}.\n\\end{equation}\nIn particular \\(\\eta\\ge0\\), and \\(\\eta=0\\) if and only if\n\\(\\mathcal L(X)=\\rho_1:=\\frac12(\\delta_{-1}+\\delta_1)\\).\n\\end{lemma}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nExpanding \\(Q_2^2\\) and using \\(\\EE X=0\\), \\(\\EE X^2=1\\), and\n\\(\\EE X^3=\\beta_3\\) gives\n\\[\n\\kappa\n=\\EE[(X^2-1-\\beta_3X)^2]\n=\\EE[(X^2-1)^2]-\\beta_3^2\n=\\EE X^4-1-\\beta_3^2.\n\\]\nSubstitution gives \\eqref{eq:appendix-normalized-fourth-moment-algebra}.\nThe first displayed form of \\(\\eta\\) proves non-negativity.  If\n\\(\\eta=0\\), then \\(\\beta_3=0\\) and \\(Q_2=0\\) almost surely, hence\n\\(X^2=1\\) almost surely; since \\(\\EE X=0\\), the two signs have equal mass.\nThe converse is immediate.\n\\end{proof}\n\n\\begin{lemma}[Elementary normalized \\(W_2\\) coupling]%\n\\label{lem:appendix-normalized-fourth-moment-w2-coupling}\nLet \\(X\\) be a real random variable with \\(\\EE X=0\\), \\(\\EE X^2=1\\), and\n\\(\\EE X^4\u003c\\infty\\), and define \\(\\eta\\) as in\nLemma~\\ref{lem:appendix-normalized-fourth-moment-defect-algebra}.  Then\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:appendix-normalized-sign-rademacher-coupling}\nW_2(\\mathcal L(X),\\rho_1)\n\\le 4\\eta^{1/4}+8\\eta^{1/2}.\n\\end{equation}\n\\end{lemma}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nLet\n\\[\nM:=\\EE[(X^2-1)^2].\n\\]\nThe calculation in the preceding lemma gives\n\\[\nM=\\kappa+\\beta_3^2\\le32\\eta .\n\\]\nLet \\(S=1\\) on \\(\\{X\\ge0\\}\\) and \\(S=-1\\) on \\(\\{X\u003c0\\}\\), and write\n\\(r_p=\\mathcal L(S)=p\\delta_1+(1-p)\\delta_{-1}\\).  For every real \\(x\\),\nwith this convention at \\(x=0\\),\n\\[\n|x-\\operatorname{sgn}x|\\le |x^2-1|.\n\\]\nIndeed \\(|x^2-1|=|x-1|(x+1)\\) for \\(x\\ge0\\), and\n\\(|x^2-1|=|x+1|(1-x)\\) for \\(x\u003c0\\).  Coupling \\(X\\) and \\(S\\) on the same\nprobability space gives\n\\begin{equation}\\label{eq:appendix-couple-x-to-sign}\nW_2(\\mathcal L(X),r_p)\n\\le \\bigl(\\EE|X-S|^2\\bigr)^{1/2}\n\\le M^{1/2}.\n\\end{equation}\n\nIt remains to couple the biased sign law to the symmetric Rademacher law.\nOn the two-point set \\(\\{-1,1\\}\\), optimal quadratic transport moves the\nexcess mass \\(|p-\\frac12|\\) across distance \\(2\\), so\n\\[\nW_2(r_p,\\rho_1)^2=4\\left|p-\\frac12\\right|.\n\\]\nSince \\(\\EE X=0\\),\n\\[\n2p-1=\\EE S=\\EE(S-X),\n\\]\nand Cauchy--Schwarz together with\n\\eqref{eq:appendix-couple-x-to-sign} gives\n\\[\n\\left|p-\\frac12\\right|\n\\le \\frac12\\EE|S-X|\n\\le \\frac12 M^{1/2}.\n\\]\nConsequently\n\\[\nW_2(r_p,\\rho_1)\\le \\sqrt2\\,M^{1/4}.\n\\]\nThe triangle inequality now yields\n\\[\nW_2(\\mathcal L(X),\\rho_1)\n\\le M^{1/2}+\\sqrt2\\,M^{1/4}\n\\le \\sqrt{32}\\,\\eta^{1/2}+\\sqrt2\\,32^{1/4}\\eta^{1/4}.\n\\]\nSince \\(\\sqrt{32}\u003c8\\) and \\(\\sqrt2\\,32^{1/4}=2^{7/4}\u003c4\\), this proves\n\\eqref{eq:appendix-normalized-sign-rademacher-coupling}.\n\\end{proof}\n\nFor a law \\(\\nu\\) with mean \\(\\bar\\gamma\\) and variance \\(\\sigma^2\u003e0\\), set\n\\(X=(\\gamma-\\bar\\gamma)/\\sigma\\), let\n\\(\\nu_c=(\\gamma-\\bar\\gamma)_\\#\\nu\\), and put\n\\(\\rho_\\sigma=\\frac12(\\delta_{-\\sigma}+\\delta_\\sigma)\\).  Quadratic\nWasserstein distance is homogeneous under dilation:\n\\[\nW_2\\bigl((x\\mapsto ax)_\\#\\mu,(x\\mapsto ax)_\\#\\rho\\bigr)\n=|a|\\,W_2(\\mu,\\rho).\n\\]\nDefine\n\\[\n\\Delta_6(\\nu)\n:=\\sigma^6\\left(\n\\frac{\\beta_3^2}{32}+\\frac{\\EE(X^2-1-\\beta_3X)^2}{8}\n\\right).\n\\]\nCombining this dilation identity with the normalized lemma gives exactly the\nestimate used in the main text,\n\\[\nW_2(\\nu_c,\\rho_\\sigma)\n\\le\n4\\,\\sigma^{-1/2}\\Delta_6(\\nu)^{1/4}\n+8\\,\\sigma^{-2}\\Delta_6(\\nu)^{1/2},\n\\]\nEquality \\(\\Delta_6(\\nu)=0\\) is equivalent to the symmetric two-point centred\nlaw.  Thus the appendix supplies a self-contained algebraic coupling proof,\nnot an additional finite-time stability theorem.\n\n\\section{Weighted trigonometric normalization}%\n\\label{app:entropy-integrals}\n\\label{app:background-symbol-criterion}\n\nThis appendix records the change of variables behind the Laurent coefficient\nnormalization.  Set \\(y=\\tan\\theta\\),\n\\(-\\pi/2\u003c\\theta\u003c\\pi/2\\).  Then\n\\[\n  \\frac{\\dd y}{\\pi(1+y^2)}=\\frac{\\dd\\theta}{\\pi}.\n\\]\nWith \\(z=e^{2\\ii\\theta}\\),\n\\[\n  \\cos(2k\\theta)=\\frac{z^k+z^{-k}}2,\\qquad\n  \\sin(2k\\theta)=\\frac{z^k-z^{-k}}{2\\ii}.\n\\]\nThus the Cauchy mode integrals in\nTheorem~\\ref{thm:finite-fourier-mode-integral-algorithm} are exactly Haar\nconstant terms:\n\\[\n  \\int_{\\RR}\\prod_j u_{n_j}(y)\\,\\omega(\\dd y)\n  =[z^0]\\prod_j Q_{n_j}(z).\n\\]\nFor order eight, Appendix~\\ref{app:order-eight-laurent-certificate} records\nthe row certificate as a finite coefficient-calculus check.\n\n\\fi\n\n\\section{Auxiliary order-eight Laurent coefficient certificate}%\n\\label{app:order-eight-laurent-certificate}\n\nThis appendix gives the finite certificate for the order-eight rows used to\naudit the \\(A_8\\) substitution.  The main coefficient hierarchy has already\nbeen proved in Section~\\ref{sec:entropy-asymptotics}; the material below is\na reproducible check of one explicit example.  The single convention is\n\\[\nq_{n,k}=2^{-n}(-\\ii)^n\n\\operatorname{sgn}(k)^{\\,n\\bmod2}\n\\binom{n-1}{|k|-1},\n\\qquad 0\u003c|k|\\le n,\n\\]\nand\n\\[\nJ(n_1,\\ldots,n_r)=[z^0]\\prod_{j=1}^rQ_{n_j}(z).\n\\]\n\nThe Laurent representatives used in the rows through total order eight are\n\\begin{align}\nQ_2(z)\n\u0026=-\\frac14\\bigl(z+z^{-1}+z^2+z^{-2}\\bigr),\n\\label{eq:appendix-d-explicit-q2}\\\\\nQ_3(z)\n\u0026=\\frac{\\ii}{8}\\bigl((z-z^{-1})+2(z^2-z^{-2})+(z^3-z^{-3})\\bigr),\n\\label{eq:appendix-d-explicit-q3}\\\\\nQ_4(z)\n\u0026=\\frac1{16}\\bigl((z+z^{-1})+3(z^2+z^{-2})\n  +3(z^3+z^{-3})+(z^4+z^{-4})\\bigr),\n\\label{eq:appendix-d-explicit-q4}\\\\\nQ_5(z)\n\u0026=-\\frac{\\ii}{32}\\bigl((z-z^{-1})+4(z^2-z^{-2})\n  +6(z^3-z^{-3})+4(z^4-z^{-4})+(z^5-z^{-5})\\bigr),\n\\label{eq:appendix-d-explicit-q5}\\\\\nQ_6(z)\n\u0026=-\\frac1{64}\\bigl((z+z^{-1})+5(z^2+z^{-2})\n  +10(z^3+z^{-3})+10(z^4+z^{-4}) \\nonumber\\\\\n\u0026\\hspace{6.7em}\n  +5(z^5+z^{-5})+(z^6+z^{-6})\\bigr).\n\\label{eq:appendix-d-explicit-q6}\n\\end{align}\nThese are exactly the cases \\(2\\le n\\le6\\) of\n\\eqref{eq:mode-laurent-polynomial-definition}.  They are displayed so that\nthe signs in the odd negative-exponent rows can be checked directly.\n\nFor a Laurent polynomial \\(F(z)=\\sum_{|k|\\le K}a_kz^k\\), put\n\\[\n\\mathsf G_N(F):=\\frac1N\\sum_{\\ell=0}^{N-1}F(\\zeta_N^\\ell),\n\\qquad \\zeta_N:=e^{2\\pi\\ii/N}.\n\\]\nIf \\(N\u003eK\\), then \\(\\mathsf G_N(F)=[z^0]F\\).  Thus the following exact\nroot-of-unity checks extract the same constant terms without using the\nzero-sum recurrence:\n\\[\n\\begin{array}{c|c}\n\\text{object}\u0026\\text{value}\\\\\n\\hline\nQ_2(1),Q_2(-1)\u0026-1,\\ 0\\\\\nQ_3(1),Q_3(-1)\u00260,\\ 0\\\\\nQ_4(1),Q_4(-1)\u00261,\\ 0\\\\\nQ_5(1),Q_5(-1)\u00260,\\ 0\\\\\nQ_6(1),Q_6(-1)\u0026-1,\\ 0\\\\\n\\mathsf G_{17}(Q_2Q_6)\u00263/64\\\\\n\\mathsf G_{17}(Q_3Q_5)\u0026-15/128\\\\\n\\mathsf G_{17}(Q_2Q_3^2)\u0026-9/128 .\n\\end{array}\n\\]\nThe grid checks are exact finite averages, since\n\\(17\u003e2+6=3+5=2+3+3\\).\n\n\\begin{lemma}[Deterministic exact Laurent recurrence]%\n\\label{lem:appendix-d-deterministic-laurent-recurrence}\nLet \\(\\mathbf n=(n_1,\\ldots,n_r)\\) be any finite row of positive integers.\nDefine finitely supported maps \\(C_j:\\ZZ\\to\\QQ[\\ii]\\) by\n\\[\nC_0(s)=\\mathbf 1_{\\{s=0\\}},\\qquad\nC_j(s)=\\sum_{0\u003c|k|\\le n_j}\n2^{-n_j}(-\\ii)^{n_j}\\operatorname{sgn}(k)^{\\,n_j\\bmod2}\n\\binom{n_j-1}{|k|-1}\\,C_{j-1}(s-k).\n\\]\nThen\n\\[\n  C_r(0)=[z^0]\\prod_{j=1}^r Q_{n_j}(z)=J(\\mathbf n).\n\\]\nEquivalently, with\n\\[\n\\mathcal K(\\mathbf n)\n:=\\{(k_1,\\ldots,k_r):0\u003c|k_j|\\le n_j,\\ k_1+\\cdots+k_r=0\\}\n\\]\nand \\(\\lambda_n:=2^{-n}(-\\ii)^n\\),\n\\[\nC_r(0)=\n\\prod_{j=1}^r\\lambda_{n_j}\n\\sum_{\\mathbf k\\in\\mathcal K(\\mathbf n)}\n\\prod_{j=1}^r\n\\operatorname{sgn}(k_j)^{\\,n_j\\bmod2}\n\\binom{n_j-1}{|k_j|-1}.\n\\]\n\\end{lemma}\n\n\\begin{proof}\nThe coefficient formula \\eqref{eq:mode-laurent-coefficients} says that\nmultiplication by \\(Q_{n_j}\\) sends a coefficient array \\(C_{j-1}\\) to the\nconvolution array displayed above.  Induction on \\(j\\) gives\n\\[\n  C_j(s)=[z^s]\\prod_{a=1}^jQ_{n_a}(z),\n\\]\nand hence \\(C_r(0)\\) is the desired constant term.  Expanding the last\ncoefficient and collecting the common factor\n\\(\\prod_j\\lambda_{n_j}\\) gives the zero-sum formula.\n\\end{proof}\n\nThe row certificate is the following finite table: \\(S(\\mathbf n)\\) is the\ninteger zero-sum convolution in\nLemma~\\ref{lem:appendix-d-deterministic-laurent-recurrence}, and\n\\(J(\\mathbf n)=\\Lambda(\\mathbf n)S(\\mathbf n)\\), where\n\\(\\Lambda(\\mathbf n)=\\prod_j\\lambda_{n_j}\\).\n\\[\n\\begin{array}{c|r|r|c|c}\n\\mathbf n\u0026|\\mathcal K(\\mathbf n)|\u0026S(\\mathbf n)\u0026\\Lambda(\\mathbf n)\u0026J(\\mathbf n)\\\\\n\\hline\n(2,6)\u00264\u002612\u00261/256\u00263/64\\\\\n(3,5)\u00266\u0026-30\u00261/256\u0026-15/128\\\\\n(4,4)\u00268\u002640\u00261/256\u00265/32\\\\\n(2,2,4)\u002612\u002624\u00261/256\u00263/32\\\\\n(2,3,3)\u002614\u0026-18\u00261/256\u0026-9/128\\\\\n(2,2,2,2)\u002636\u002636\u00261/256\u00269/64 .\n\\end{array}\n\\]\nOdd total-order entries through order eight vanish by\n\\(u_n(-y)=(-1)^nu_n(y)\\).  The sign-sensitive rows\n\\((3,5)\\) and \\((2,3,3)\\) use the same all-sign coefficient rule as the\nother rows; no separate conjugation convention is applied.\n\nAs a model for the sign-sensitive rows, write\n\\[\nw_n(k):=\\operatorname{sgn}(k)^{\\,n\\bmod 2}\n\\binom{n-1}{|k|-1},\\qquad 0\u003c|k|\\le n .\n\\]\nFor \\((3,5)\\), the zero-sum condition forces the second index to be \\(-k\\).\nHence\n\\[\nS(3,5)\n=\\sum_{0\u003c|k|\\le3}w_3(k)w_5(-k).\n\\]\nSince \\(\\operatorname{sgn}(-k)=-\\operatorname{sgn}(k)\\), the two choices\n\\(k=\\pm r\\), \\(r=1,2,3\\), contribute the same negative weight:\n\\[\nS(3,5)\n=-2\\left[\n\\binom20\\binom40+\\binom21\\binom41+\\binom22\\binom42\n\\right]\n=-2(1+8+6)=-30.\n\\]\nThe rational prefactor is\n\\(\\Lambda(3,5)=\\lambda_3\\lambda_5=(\\ii/8)(-\\ii/32)=1/256\\), and therefore\n\\[\nJ(3,5)=-\\frac{30}{256}=-\\frac{15}{128}.\n\\]\nThe row \\((2,3,3)\\) is obtained from the same recurrence with no change of\nsign convention.\n\nFinally, the order-eight coefficient substitution is obtained by inserting\nthe six row values into the universal entropy coefficient:\n\\[\n\\begin{aligned}\nA_8\u0026=\\mu_2\\mu_6J(2,6)+\\mu_3\\mu_5J(3,5)\n+\\frac12\\mu_4^2J(4,4)\n-\\frac12\\mu_2^2\\mu_4J(2,2,4)\\\\\n\u0026\\hspace{2.5em}\n-\\frac12\\mu_2\\mu_3^2J(2,3,3)\n+\\frac1{12}\\mu_2^4J(2,2,2,2).\n\\end{aligned}\n\\]\nWith \\(\\mu_2=\\sigma^2\\), this gives\n\\[\nA_8=\n\\frac{3\\sigma^8-12\\sigma^4\\mu_4+9\\sigma^2\\mu_3^2\n+12\\sigma^2\\mu_6-30\\mu_3\\mu_5+20\\mu_4^2}{256}.\n\\]\nThis appendix is therefore a compact reproducibility certificate for the\nfinite Laurent rows and the coefficient substitution.  It is not an\nadditional hypothesis and does not replace the main-text coefficient theorem.\n"

-\section{Related-work comparison}%
-\label{app:related-work-scope}
-
-This appendix separates the theorem statements in the paper from nearby
-results that use similar words--entropy, transport, Poisson, heat profile,
-or Hardy--Stein--for different objects.  The introduction organizes the
-closest comparisons by mathematical mechanism.  The longer table below
-records additional entropy, Sobolev--Bregman, heat-profile,
-Poisson-channel papers, Cauchy-divergence formulas, and general
-entropy-representation references.  The distinctions used in the table are
-structural: the present law \(\nu\) is fixed, the reference is the
-mean-matched harmonic Poisson/Cauchy kernel, and the coefficients are obtained
-by expanding the quotient before applying
-\(\Phi(s)=(1+s)\log(1+s)-s\).
-
-{\scriptsize
-\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}
-\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.18}
-\begin{longtable}{>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.22\linewidth}|%
->{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.24\linewidth}|%
->{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.14\linewidth}|%
->{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.32\linewidth}}
-\caption{Broader theorem-level comparison with nearby entropy, transport,
-heat-profile, Poisson-channel, and Hardy--Stein results.}
-\label{tab:broader-related-work-comparison}\\
-\textbf{our result}
-& \textbf{comparator theorem/context}
-& \textbf{source}
-& \textbf{precise separation}\\
-\hline
-Theorem~\ref{thm:main-A}: fixed-law one-dimensional matched
-Poisson/Cauchy KL coefficient hierarchy and variance threshold.
-& Entropy and log-Sobolev deficit papers, together with entropic CLT surveys,
-form part of the broader information-theoretic background.
-& \cite{NourdinPeccatiSwan2014EntropyFourthMoment,
-BobkovGozlanRobertoSamson2014LogSobolevDeficit,
-BobkovGotzeRenyiSurvey2025}
-& These papers concern entropy fourth-moment phenomena, functional-inequality
-deficits, or CLT divergence frameworks.  The present theorem instead fixes
-one input law, smooths it by the harmonic Poisson kernel, and evaluates the
-matched large-\(t\) KL coefficients by finite Laurent algebra.\\
-\hline
-Theorem~\ref{thm:main-A}: fixed-law one-dimensional matched
-Poisson/Cauchy KL coefficient hierarchy and variance threshold.
-& Esscher-transform and entropic CLT theorems compare normalized sums with
-Gaussian or stable limits, often through R{\'e}nyi/KL information and
-changing laws.
-& \cite{BobkovGotzeEsscher2025}
-& The law here is not a normalized convolution sequence.  It is one fixed
-input law smoothed by \(P_t\), and the object is the large-\(t\) scalar
-\(D_{\rm KL}(P_t*\nu\|P_t(\cdot-\bar\gamma))\), with coefficients given by
-Cayley Laurent constant terms.\\
-\hline
-Theorem~\ref{thm:main-A}: coefficient hierarchy after the centred linear
-entropy layer cancels.
-& Entropy fourth-moment and Shannon--Stam stability theorems quantify
-distance to Gaussian extremizers or CLT limits.
-& \cite{NourdinPeccatiSwan2014EntropyFourthMoment,
-EldanMikulincer2020ShannonStam,ArtsteinBallBartheNaor2004}
-& Those results control entropy deficits or convergence to Gaussian
-reference laws.  They do not expand a moving harmonic Cauchy reference, and
-the fourth-moment identity recorded here is an example of the Laurent
-coefficient calculus rather than a replacement for fourth-moment theory.\\
-\hline
-Theorem~\ref{thm:main-B}: finite-moment multidimensional radial Poisson
-quotient jet and tensor KL coefficients.
-& Large-time heat-profile theorems identify asymptotic kernels and profile
-corrections for linear heat or fractional heat flows.
-& \cite{DuoandikoetxeaZuazua1992,EscobedoZuazua1991,
-AnkerPapageorgiouZhang2023HeatSymmetricSpaces,
-Vazquez2018FractionalHeatEuclidean,
-IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017,
-IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2022RefinedFractional}
-& The comparator estimates the evolved density or kernel in norm, weighted,
-or relative-error scales.  Theorem~\ref{thm:main-B} first proves a
-two-region quotient remainder for the radial Poisson kernel and then transfers
-that quotient expansion through the nonlinear KL Taylor map.\\
-\hline
-Theorem~\ref{thm:all-order-stable-first-unmatched-moment}: first unmatched
-tensor under heavy-tailed stable smoothing.
-& Chen--Niles-Weed prove the exact first-unmatched-moment KL asymptotic under
-Gaussian smoothing, in every dimension and at every order, assuming
-sub-Gaussian tails.
-& \cite[Theorem~2.5]{ChenNilesWeed2022SmoothedWasserstein}
-& With their heat time \(t=s^2\) and \(r=n+1\), their Hermite coefficient is
-exactly the \(\alpha=2\) specialization of \(\mathcal Q_{\alpha,d,r}\).
-The first-unmatched quadratic mechanism is therefore prior work.  The present
-increment is \(0<\alpha<2\), the critical complete-moment exponent, endpoint
-sufficiency, and analytic uniform sharpness in the non-Hilbert regime; in the
-Hilbert regime the below-\(r\) obstruction is only coefficient-domain
-minimality.\\
-\hline
-Theorem~\ref{thm:main-B}: optimal uniform sufficient stable-kernel moment
-exponent.
-& Fractional-diffusion moment expansions subtract kernel derivatives and
-control the density remainder in scaled \(L^q\) and weighted \(L^1\) norms.
-& \cite{IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2017,
-IshigeKawakamiMichihisa2022RefinedFractional}
-& Those estimates do not control the matched quotient in the critical
-weighted \(L^{q_{\alpha,d}}\) space or transfer it through KL.  The critical
-translation growth yields
-\(p_{\alpha,d}=\max\{2,4(d+\alpha)/(d+\alpha+4)\}\).  This is uniform
-moment-class optimality, not a law-by-law criterion when \(d+\alpha>4\).\\
-\hline
-Theorem~\ref{thm:main-B}: the specific
-\(\mathcal R_{d,L}(t)=o(t^{-L})\) remainder condition is equivalent to the
-finite-\(L\)-moment input in the stated range.
-& Euclidean fractional-heat and Poisson-kernel profile results, including
-V{\'a}zquez's large-time fractional heat theorem, give convergence to the
-fundamental fractional profile and rates under moment assumptions.
-& \cite{Vazquez2018FractionalHeatEuclidean,
-FilaIshigeKawakami2012PoissonKernel,
-Iwabuchi2015CriticalBurgersPoisson,
-Papageorgiou2024FractionalLargeTime}
-& These results are the closest PDE large-time analogues.  They do not
-identify the matched KL coefficients, because \(L^p\) or relative-error
-profile convergence does not determine the cancellations and polynomial mode
-mixing in
-\(D_{\rm KL}(P_t*\nu\|P_t(\cdot-\bar\gamma))\).\\
-\hline
-Theorem~\ref{thm:main-C}: finite-variance domain and endpoint closure for the
-moving matched Cauchy quotient.
-& Polarized Hardy--Stein and non-JFA Sobolev--Bregman identities represent
-semigroup norm, entropy, or Sobolev differences through Dirichlet/Bregman
-forms.
-& \cite{BogdanGutowskiPietruskaPaluba2025PolarizedHardyStein,
-GutowskiKwasnicki2025BeurlingDenySobolevBregman}
-& The underlying simultaneous-semigroup Bregman differentiation is general.
-Theorem~\ref{thm:main-C} checks that the moving Cauchy quotient belongs to the
-needed compact-window domain, evaluates the annular Cauchy Green limits, and
-proves the endpoint passage to the full one-sided Bregman tail integral.\\
-\hline
-All three theorem groups: matched harmonic Poisson smoothing of a fixed
-Euclidean law.
-& Poisson transport and stationary point-process transport theorems build
-transport maps, metric structures, gradient flows, and entropy convexity on
-counting or point-process spaces.
-& \cite{LopezRiveraShenfeld2025PoissonTransport,
-ErbarHuesmannJalowyMuller2025StationaryPointTransport}
-& The Poisson object there is a count or point-process law.  Here
-\(P_t(x)=\pi^{-1}t/(t^2+x^2)\) is the harmonic Poisson kernel on \(\RR\);
-there is no point-process transport map in the proof of the KL coefficient
-hierarchy.\\
-\hline
-All three theorem groups: entropy as a scalar functional.
-& Entropy-gradient-flow and transport-inequality theorems use entropy to
-define metric or convexity structures for Markov chains, jump processes, or
-transport geometries.
-& \cite{OttoVillani2000,Maas2011EntropyMarkov,Erbar2014JumpEntropy}
-& These results give structural entropy dissipation or convexity principles.
-They are not coefficient-evaluation theorems for the fixed-law, moving
-Cauchy-reference functional
-\(D_{\rm KL}(P_t*\nu\|P_t(\cdot-\bar\gamma))\).\\
-\end{longtable}
-}
-
-Closed formulas for divergences between Cauchy laws also do not imply the
-coefficient hierarchy above.  Results such as Nielsen--Okamura
-\cite{NielsenOkamura2023Cauchy}, Nielsen
-\cite{Nielsen2020CauchyVoronoi}, and Verd{\'u}
-\cite{Verdu2023Cauchy} evaluate \(f\)-divergences or information-geometric
-quantities when both arguments are members of a finite-dimensional Cauchy
-family.  In the present problem the numerator \(P_t*\nu\) is generally a
-mixture of Cauchy translates, not a single Cauchy law; only the denominator is
-the mean-matched Cauchy kernel.  Even when a law is approximated by a nearby
-Cauchy profile, the KL coefficients are not obtained by differentiating the
-two-parameter Cauchy divergence formula: after centering, the linear term in
-the quotient integrates to zero, while the \(t^{-2m}\) coefficient collects
-all products of quotient modes whose total order is \(2m\) through the
-nonlinear series for \(\Phi\).  The fixed-law hierarchy is therefore a
-moment-polynomial constant-term calculation for a Cauchy mixture quotient,
-not an expansion inside the Cauchy statistical manifold.
-
-The regularly varying boundary theorem uses Karamata theory in a different
-role from stable-limit entropy theory.  The integrated slow-variation facts
-and direct/tail integral theorems are classical
-\cite{BinghamGoldieTeugels1987RegularVariation}; they identify the truncated
-moment and control the local and far parts of the Cayley quotient.  Entropic
-convergence to stable laws and stable de Bruijn or fractional-information
-identities
-\cite{BobkovChistyakovGotze2013StableEntropy,Johnson2013StableDeBruijn,
-Toscani2016StableEntropy} instead concern normalized convolution sequences,
-stable interpolation, or entropy dissipation relative to a stable target.
-They do not give the coefficient-subtracted, moving-Cauchy-reference
-asymptotic of
-Theorem~\ref{cor:main-body-conditional-missing-top-moment-tail}.  The new
-step is the distribution-level \(L^\infty\cap L^1(\omega)\) quotient jet at
-the exact divergent moment boundary and its transfer to the signed
-\(t^{-2N}\ell_L(t)\) residual.  Karamata's theorem itself is cited as an
-external input and is not reproved here.
-
-The Poisson terminology also hides adjacent but different entropy theories.
-Poisson-channel papers such as Guo--Shamai--Verd{\'u}
-\cite{GuoShamaiVerdu2008PoissonChannel} and Atar--Weissman
-\cite{AtarWeissman2012PoissonChannel} study conditional count outputs
-\(Y|X\sim{\rm Poisson}(\gamma X)\) or continuous-time counting processes and
-relate mutual information, relative entropy, and estimation loss.  These are
-count-output models rather than harmonic smoothing by \(P_t\), so they do not
-produce the quotient expansion used in Theorems~\ref{thm:main-A}
-and~\ref{thm:main-B}.
-
-Small-time heat-kernel entropy expansions have a different limiting regime.
-For example, the expansions of
-Menkovski--Portegies--Ravelonanosy
-\cite{MenkovskiPortegiesRavelonanosy2024HeatKernelEntropy} treat the
-relative entropy between a heat kernel and normalized Riemannian volume as the
-heat time tends to zero; the coefficients are universal local geometric
-invariants of the underlying manifold.  By contrast, here \(t\to\infty\), the
-underlying space is Euclidean, the reference is the translated harmonic
-Poisson/Cauchy kernel \(P_t(\cdot-\bar\gamma)\), and the coefficients depend
-on the fixed input law only through its centred moments and the Cayley Laurent
-constant-term rule.  Process and discretization entropy asymptotics, such as
-Fageot--Fallah--Horel
-\cite{FageotFallahHorel2022EntropicCompressibilityLevy} and
-Ghourchian--Amini--Gohari
-\cite{GhourchianAminiGohari2018InnovationCompressibility}, concern
-compressibility or innovation limits rather than a single fixed law smoothed
-by a harmonic semigroup.  General representation formulas, including the
-Gibbs--Donsker--Varadhan variational formula
-\cite{DonskerVaradhan1975AsymptoticI,DupuisEllis1997WeakConvergence} and
-semigroup de Bruijn identities such as
-\cite{DeBruijn1953,HirataNemotoYoshida2012IntegralRepresentation,
-Yoshida2017RelativeEntropyDiffusion}, identify entropy through optimization
-or dissipation.  They are structural identities, not coefficient evaluations
-for the matched large-\(t\) functional in
-\eqref{eq:intro-main-functional}.
-
-\section{Fourth-moment coefficient-calculus example}%
-\label{app:optional-fourth-moment-coefficient-algebra}
-\label{app:fourth-moment-coupling-proof}
-
-The fourth-moment material is not used in the three main theorems.  Its role
-is only to illustrate how the sixth-order coefficient \(A_6\) can be read as
-a simple algebraic defect after normalizing to unit variance.  The proof
-below supplies the elementary coupling estimate underlying the
-fourth-moment discussion; it uses no finite-time KL estimate and no
-eighth-order coefficient.
-
-\begin{lemma}[Normalized fourth-moment defect algebra]%
-\label{lem:appendix-normalized-fourth-moment-defect-algebra}
-Let \(X\) be a real random variable with \(\EE X=0\), \(\EE X^2=1\), and
-\(\EE X^4<\infty\).  Put
-\[
-\beta_3=\EE X^3,\qquad
-Q_2=X^2-1-\beta_3X,\qquad
-\kappa=\EE Q_2^2,\qquad
-\eta=\frac{\beta_3^2}{32}+\frac{\kappa}{8}.
-\]
-Then
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:appendix-normalized-fourth-moment-algebra}
-\eta
-=\frac{\beta_3^2}{32}+\frac{\EE(X^2-1-\beta_3X)^2}{8}
-=\frac{\EE X^4-1}{8}-\frac{3\beta_3^2}{32}.
-\end{equation}
-In particular \(\eta\ge0\), and \(\eta=0\) if and only if
-\(\mathcal L(X)=\rho_1:=\frac12(\delta_{-1}+\delta_1)\).
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Expanding \(Q_2^2\) and using \(\EE X=0\), \(\EE X^2=1\), and
-\(\EE X^3=\beta_3\) gives
-\[
-\kappa
-=\EE[(X^2-1-\beta_3X)^2]
-=\EE[(X^2-1)^2]-\beta_3^2
-=\EE X^4-1-\beta_3^2.
-\]
-Substitution gives \eqref{eq:appendix-normalized-fourth-moment-algebra}.
-The first displayed form of \(\eta\) proves non-negativity.  If
-\(\eta=0\), then \(\beta_3=0\) and \(Q_2=0\) almost surely, hence
-\(X^2=1\) almost surely; since \(\EE X=0\), the two signs have equal mass.
-The converse is immediate.
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{lemma}[Elementary normalized \(W_2\) coupling]%
-\label{lem:appendix-normalized-fourth-moment-w2-coupling}
-Let \(X\) be a real random variable with \(\EE X=0\), \(\EE X^2=1\), and
-\(\EE X^4<\infty\), and define \(\eta\) as in
-Lemma~\ref{lem:appendix-normalized-fourth-moment-defect-algebra}.  Then
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:appendix-normalized-sign-rademacher-coupling}
-W_2(\mathcal L(X),\rho_1)
-\le 4\eta^{1/4}+8\eta^{1/2}.
-\end{equation}
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Let
-\[
-M:=\EE[(X^2-1)^2].
-\]
-The calculation in the preceding lemma gives
-\[
-M=\kappa+\beta_3^2\le32\eta .
-\]
-Let \(S=1\) on \(\{X\ge0\}\) and \(S=-1\) on \(\{X<0\}\), and write
-\(r_p=\mathcal L(S)=p\delta_1+(1-p)\delta_{-1}\).  For every real \(x\),
-with this convention at \(x=0\),
-\[
-|x-\operatorname{sgn}x|\le |x^2-1|.
-\]
-Indeed \(|x^2-1|=|x-1|(x+1)\) for \(x\ge0\), and
-\(|x^2-1|=|x+1|(1-x)\) for \(x<0\).  Coupling \(X\) and \(S\) on the same
-probability space gives
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:appendix-couple-x-to-sign}
-W_2(\mathcal L(X),r_p)
-\le \bigl(\EE|X-S|^2\bigr)^{1/2}
-\le M^{1/2}.
-\end{equation}
-
-It remains to couple the biased sign law to the symmetric Rademacher law.
-On the two-point set \(\{-1,1\}\), optimal quadratic transport moves the
-excess mass \(|p-\frac12|\) across distance \(2\), so
-\[
-W_2(r_p,\rho_1)^2=4\left|p-\frac12\right|.
-\]
-Since \(\EE X=0\),
-\[
-2p-1=\EE S=\EE(S-X),
-\]
-and Cauchy--Schwarz together with
-\eqref{eq:appendix-couple-x-to-sign} gives
-\[
-\left|p-\frac12\right|
-\le \frac12\EE|S-X|
-\le \frac12 M^{1/2}.
-\]
-Consequently
-\[
-W_2(r_p,\rho_1)\le \sqrt2\,M^{1/4}.
-\]
-The triangle inequality now yields
-\[
-W_2(\mathcal L(X),\rho_1)
-\le M^{1/2}+\sqrt2\,M^{1/4}
-\le \sqrt{32}\,\eta^{1/2}+\sqrt2\,32^{1/4}\eta^{1/4}.
-\]
-Since \(\sqrt{32}<8\) and \(\sqrt2\,32^{1/4}=2^{7/4}<4\), this proves
-\eqref{eq:appendix-normalized-sign-rademacher-coupling}.
-\end{proof}
-
-For a law \(\nu\) with mean \(\bar\gamma\) and variance \(\sigma^2>0\), set
-\(X=(\gamma-\bar\gamma)/\sigma\), let
-\(\nu_c=(\gamma-\bar\gamma)_\#\nu\), and put
-\(\rho_\sigma=\frac12(\delta_{-\sigma}+\delta_\sigma)\).  Quadratic
-Wasserstein distance is homogeneous under dilation:
-\[
-W_2\bigl((x\mapsto ax)_\#\mu,(x\mapsto ax)_\#\rho\bigr)
-=|a|\,W_2(\mu,\rho).
-\]
-Define
-\[
-\Delta_6(\nu)
-:=\sigma^6\left(
-\frac{\beta_3^2}{32}+\frac{\EE(X^2-1-\beta_3X)^2}{8}
-\right).
-\]
-Combining this dilation identity with the normalized lemma gives exactly the
-estimate used in the main text,
-\[
-W_2(\nu_c,\rho_\sigma)
-\le
-4\,\sigma^{-1/2}\Delta_6(\nu)^{1/4}
-+8\,\sigma^{-2}\Delta_6(\nu)^{1/2},
-\]
-Equality \(\Delta_6(\nu)=0\) is equivalent to the symmetric two-point centred
-law.  Thus the appendix supplies a self-contained algebraic coupling proof,
-not an additional finite-time stability theorem.
-
-\section{Weighted trigonometric normalization}%
-\label{app:entropy-integrals}
-\label{app:background-symbol-criterion}
-
-This appendix records the change of variables behind the Laurent coefficient
-normalization.  Set \(y=\tan\theta\),
-\(-\pi/2<\theta<\pi/2\).  Then
-\[
-  \frac{\dd y}{\pi(1+y^2)}=\frac{\dd\theta}{\pi}.
-\]
-With \(z=e^{2\ii\theta}\),
-\[
-  \cos(2k\theta)=\frac{z^k+z^{-k}}2,\qquad
-  \sin(2k\theta)=\frac{z^k-z^{-k}}{2\ii}.
-\]
-Thus the Cauchy mode integrals in
-Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-fourier-mode-integral-algorithm} are exactly Haar
-constant terms:
-\[
-  \int_{\RR}\prod_j u_{n_j}(y)\,\omega(\dd y)
-  =[z^0]\prod_j Q_{n_j}(z).
-\]
-For order eight, Appendix~\ref{app:order-eight-laurent-certificate} records
-the row certificate as a finite coefficient-calculus check.
-
-\fi

-\label{thm:low-dimensional-finite-covariance-threshold}
-Let \(1\le d\le3\), and let \(\nu\) be a probability law on \(\RR^d\) with
-finite mean.  With
-\[
- H_d(t)=D_{\rm KL}\!\left(P_t^{(d)}*\nu\,\middle\|\,
- P_t^{(d)}(\mathord\cdot-\bar\gamma)\right),
-\]
-one has
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:low-dimensional-covariance-iff}
- \EE|X|^2<\infty
- \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
- \limsup_{t\to\infty}t^4H_d(t)<\infty.
-\end{equation}
-If the covariance is finite, then
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:low-dimensional-covariance-limit}
- H_d(t)=\mathcal Q_d(\Sigma)t^{-4}+o(t^{-4}).
-\end{equation}
-If it is infinite, then \(t^4H_d(t)\to+\infty\) in the extended sense.
-\end{theorem}
-
-\begin{proof}
-For \(d\le3\), \(q_d=2\).  Thus Theorem
-\ref{thm:multidim-l2-moment-threshold} and the \(L^2\) alternative in
-Theorem~\ref{thm:second-order-quotient-kl-coefficient} prove
-\eqref{eq:low-dimensional-covariance-limit}.  The entropy representation is
-valid in the extended sense by change of variables; for large \(t\), the
-\(L^2\) convergence makes \(\Phi(\delta_t^{(d)})\) integrable because
-\(\Phi(s)\le C s^2\) on \([-1,\infty)\).
-
-Conversely, if \(\EE|X|^2=\infty\), some unit vector \(e\) satisfies
-\(\EE(e\cdot X)^2=\infty\).  Projection onto \(e\) sends the radial
-\(d\)-dimensional Poisson law to the one-dimensional Cauchy law at the same
-scale.  The data-processing inequality and
-Theorem~\ref{thm:sharp-leading-kl-variance-threshold} therefore give
-\[
- H_d(t)\ge
- D_{\rm KL}(P_t*\nu_e\|P_t(\mathord\cdot-\bar\gamma_e)),
-\]
-whose product with \(t^4\) tends to \(+\infty\).
-\end{proof}
-
-\begin{proposition}[Finite covariance does not control high-dimensional KL]
-\label{prop:high-dimensional-finite-covariance-obstruction}
-For every \(d\ge4\), there exists a centred discrete probability law on
-\(\RR^d\) with positive-definite finite covariance such that
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:high-dimensional-finite-covariance-obstruction}
- \limsup_{t\to\infty}t^4H_d(t)=+\infty.
-\end{equation}
-\end{proposition}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Choose positive \(\alpha_j\) with \(\sum_j\alpha_j<\infty\), radii
-\(R_j\uparrow\infty\), and weights
-\(w_j=\alpha_jR_j^{-2}\).  After rescaling the sequence if necessary,
-\(W=\sum_jw_j<1\).  Begin with
-\[
- (1-W)\delta_0+\sum_{j\ge1}\frac{w_j}{2}
- (\delta_{R_je_1}+\delta_{-R_je_1}),
-\]
-and transfer an arbitrarily small amount of the mass at zero to a bounded
-centred symmetric law spanning \(\RR^d\).  The covariance is then positive
-definite and finite because \(\sum_jw_jR_j^2=\sum_j\alpha_j<\infty\).
-
-Fix a sufficiently small constant \(\kappa>0\), and set
-\[
- t_j=\kappa R_jw_j^{1/(d+1)}.
-\]
-The radii may be chosen recursively so that \(t_j\to\infty\).  Let \(A_j\)
-be the ball of radius \(t_j\) centred at \(R_je_1\).  The \(j\)th mixture
-component gives
-\[
- (P_{t_j}^{(d)}*\nu)(A_j)\ge c_dw_j,
-\]
-whereas, since \(t_j/R_j\to0\), the centred reference satisfies
-\[
- P_{t_j}^{(d)}(A_j)
- \le C_d(t_j/R_j)^{d+1}
- =C_d\kappa^{d+1}w_j.
-\]
-Choose \(\kappa\) so that the second constant is strictly smaller than the
-first.  Data processing to the partition \(\{A_j,A_j^c\}\) and
-Lemma~\ref{lem:bernoulli-kl-linear-separation} then give
-\(H_d(t_j)\ge c'_dw_j\).  Hence
-\[
- t_j^4H_d(t_j)
- \ge c''_dR_j^4w_j^{1+4/(d+1)}
- =c''_d\alpha_j^{1+4/(d+1)}
- R_j^{2(d-3)/(d+1)}.
-\]
-The exponent of \(R_j\) is positive exactly when \(d>3\).  Choosing the
-radii recursively makes the final expression tend to infinity.
-\end{proof}
-
-For the high-dimensional entropy topology, define
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:critical-kl-exponents}
- q_d:=\frac{d+5}{d+1},
- \qquad
- p_d:=\frac{4(d+1)}{d+5}.
-\end{equation}
-Thus \(1<q_d<2\), \(2<p_d<4\), and \(p_dq_d=4\) when \(d\ge4\).
-
-\begin{lemma}[Critical translation remainder]
-\label{lem:critical-lq-translation-remainder}
-Let \(d\ge4\), let \(p_d,q_d\) be as in
-\eqref{eq:critical-kl-exponents}, and put \(m=\lfloor p_d\rfloor\).
-If \(T_m(y,z)\) is the Taylor polynomial of \(F_y(z)\) through degree
-\(m\), then
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:critical-lq-exact-translation-norm}
- \|F_\cdot(z)\|_{L^{q_d}(\Omega_d)}^{q_d}
- =1+\frac{2(d+5)}{(d+1)(d+3)}|z|^2
- +\frac{3}{(d+1)(d+3)}|z|^4.
-\end{equation}
-Consequently, for a constant depending only on \(d\),
-\begin{equation}\label{eq:critical-lq-global-remainder}
- \|F_\cdot(z)-T_m(\cdot,z)\|_{L^{q_d}(\Omega_d)}
- \le C_d
- \begin{cases}
- |z|^{m+1},& |z|\le1,\\
- |z|^{p_d},& |z|>1,
- \end{cases}
- \le C_d|z|^{p_d}.
-\end{equation}
-Here \(m=2\) for \(4\le d\le10\), while \(m=3\) for \(d\ge11\),
-including the integer endpoint \(p_{11}=3\).
-\end{lemma}
-
-\begin{proof}
-Since \(a(q_d-1)=2\), translation by \(z\) gives
-\[
- \|F_\cdot(z)\|_{q_d}^{q_d}
- =c_d\int_{\RR^d}
- \frac{(1+|u+z|^2)^2}{(1+|u|^2)^{(d+5)/2}}\dd u.
-\]
-Write \(A=1+|u|^2\).  The odd term in the expansion of
-\((A+|z|^2+2u\cdot z)^2\) integrates to zero, and rotational invariance
-gives
-\[
- \int(u\cdot z)^2(1+|u|^2)^{-(d+5)/2}\dd u
- =\frac{|z|^2}{d}\int |u|^2(1+|u|^2)^{-(d+5)/2}\dd u.
-\]
-The three normalized beta integrals needed here are
-\[
- \begin{aligned}
- c_d\int(1+|u|^2)^{-(d+1)/2}\dd u&=1,\\
- c_d\int(1+|u|^2)^{-(d+3)/2}\dd u&=\frac1{d+1},\\
- c_d\int(1+|u|^2)^{-(d+5)/2}\dd u
- &=\frac3{(d+1)(d+3)}.
- \end{aligned}
-\]
-Substitution proves \eqref{eq:critical-lq-exact-translation-norm}.
-
-For \(|z|\le1\), the local quotient--Taylor estimate
-\eqref{eq:local-multidim-taylor-remainder} implies the first line of
-\eqref{eq:critical-lq-global-remainder}.  For \(|z|>1\), the exact identity
-gives \(\|F_\cdot(z)\|_{q_d}\le C_d|z|^{4/q_d}=C_d|z|^{p_d}\).
-Every coefficient of \(T_m\) is bounded in \(y\), and \(m\le p_d\), so
-\(\|T_m(\cdot,z)\|_{q_d}\le C_d|z|^{p_d}\).  Finally,
-\(m+1>p_d\), which proves the last inequality for \(|z|\le1\).
-\end{proof}
